msgflow_xml_and_esql_schema.overview:
Mandatory rules for authoring correct .msgflow XML and .esql files. All rules are grounded in evidence — either from real ACE projects in this workspace, from the ACE 13.0.x schema at: /Applications/IBM App Connect Enterprise/common/schemas/MessageFlow/MessageFlow.xsd or from the official IBM documentation at: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/app-connect/13.0.x
NEVER guess attribute names, terminal names, or ESQL paths. Every value in this document has been verified. Follow every rule exactly.
KNOWN ERRORS THIS FILE PREVENTS: "Feature 'nodes' not found" → MF-01, MF-02, MF-03 "Unset mandatory property Web service URL" → MF-08b (URLSpecifier, not webServiceURL) "Can not locate timeout terminal" → MF-08b (timeout not on HTTP Request) "Unable to locate URN esql://routine/#..." → MF-08c (duplicate module names) Query string always NULL in ESQL → MF-06b (parseQueryString="true" required)

rule.title: Root element must be ecore:EPackage with mandatory attributes
rule.description: A .msgflow file is an EMF/XMI document. The root element MUST be ecore:EPackage. The following attributes are non-negotiable on every .msgflow and .subflow file: xmi:version="2.0" xmlns:xmi="http://www.omg.org/XMI" xmlns:ecore="http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore" xmlns:eflow="http://www.ibm.com/wbi/2005/eflow" xmlns:utility="http://www.ibm.com/wbi/2005/eflow_utility" nsURI — relative path of this file inside the project (see MF-02) nsPrefix — nsURI with '/' replaced by '_' (see MF-02)
rule.template: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ecore:EPackage xmi:version="2.0" xmlns:xmi="http://www.omg.org/XMI" xmlns:ecore="http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore" xmlns:eflow="http://www.ibm.com/wbi/2005/eflow" xmlns:utility="http://www.ibm.com/wbi/2005/eflow_utility" xmlns:ComIbmWSInput.msgnode="ComIbmWSInput.msgnode" xmlns:ComIbmWSReply.msgnode="ComIbmWSReply.msgnode" xmlns:ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode="ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode" xmlns:ComIbmCompute.msgnode="ComIbmCompute.msgnode" [... one xmlns: for every node type used in this flow ...] nsURI="FlowName.msgflow" nsPrefix="FlowName.msgflow">

rule.title: nsURI and nsPrefix must reflect the file's relative path inside the project
rule.description: nsURI = file path relative to the project root. nsPrefix = nsURI with every '/' replaced by '_'. The '.' in the filename is kept as-is.

rule.title: Every node type used in the flow MUST have its own xmlns: declaration on the root element
rule.description:
ACE Toolkit parses node types by looking up the xmlns prefix on the root ecore:EPackage. If a node's type prefix is missing, ACE throws "Feature 'nodes' not found" and refuses to open the flow.
For every built-in node type add: xmlns:NodeType="NodeType" For every subflow reference add: xmlns:path_to_SubFlow.subflow="path/to/SubFlow.subflow" (replace '/' with '_' in the prefix, keep '.' as-is)
Subflow Input (eflow:FCMSource) and Subflow Output (eflow:FCMSink) use the eflow: namespace already declared — they do NOT need an additional xmlns: entry.

rule.title: eClassifiers structure must wrap all nodes and connections
rule.description: Directly inside ecore:EPackage there MUST be exactly one eClassifiers element. nodes and connections live inside composition. eStructuralFeatures (for subflow UDPs) appear before translation. propertyOrganizer and stickyBoard MUST appear after composition.
rule.template:
<eClassifiers xmi:type="eflow:FCMComposite" name="FCMComposite_1"> <eSuperTypes href="http://www.ibm.com/wbi/2005/eflow#//FCMBlock"/>
<!-- eStructuralFeatures only needed for subflows with configurable UDPs --> <eStructuralFeatures xmi:type="ecore:EAttribute" xmi:id="Property.MyProperty" name="MyProperty" defaultValueLiteral=""> <eType xmi:type="ecore:EDataType" href="http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore#//EString"/> </eStructuralFeatures>
<translation xmi:type="utility:TranslatableString" key="FlowName" bundleName="FlowName" pluginId="ProjectName"/> <colorGraphic16 xmi:type="utility:GIFFileGraphic" resourceName="platform:/plugin/ProjectName/icons/full/obj16/FlowName.gif"/> <colorGraphic32 xmi:type="utility:GIFFileGraphic" resourceName="platform:/plugin/ProjectName/icons/full/obj30/FlowName.gif"/> <composition> <!-- nodes then connections here --> </composition> <propertyOrganizer/> <stickyBoard/> </eClassifiers>

field_rules.rule: key in translation = flow filename without extension e.g. "CurrentWeather"
bundleName = subfolder/FlowName when file is in a subfolder, else just FlowName

rule.title: Every nodes element must have xmi:type, xmi:id, location, and a translation child
rule.description: xmi:type = registered xmlns prefix + ":FCMComposite_1" for all regular nodes. Exceptions: Subflow Input = eflow:FCMSource, Subflow Output = eflow:FCMSink. xmi:id must be unique within the file. location = canvas x,y coordinates used by the visual editor.

rule.title: Compute node computeExpression must use exact esql://routine/ format
rule.description:
Format: esql://routine/BROKERSC HEMA#ModuleName.Main
- Root-level ESQL file (no BROKER SCHEMA statement in file): computeExpression="esql://routine/#ModuleName.Main" - ESQL in gen/ subfolder (BROKER SCHEMA gen in file): computeExpression="esql://routine/gen#ModuleName.Main"
computeMode values: "destinationAndMessage" — all normal transform/route modules (default) "exception" — modules that run only on exception paths

example.note: gen/ folder ESQL, broker schema gen

rule.title: HTTP Input node — accessing query parameters requires parseQueryString="true"
rule.description:
SOURCE OF TRUTH: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/app-connect/13.0.x?topic=nodes-httpinput-node Section: "Parse Query String" property.
By default, the HTTP Input node (ComIbmWSInput.msgnode) does NOT parse the URL query string into individual elements in the LocalEnvironment tree. The "Parse Query String" property defaults to False.
WITHOUT parseQueryString="true" on the node: InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.myParam → ALWAYS NULL Attempting to read any query parameter in ESQL will silently return NULL.
WITH parseQueryString="true" on the node: For the request GET /path?location=London&units=metric ACE URL-decodes the query string (per RFC 3986) and populates: InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.location = 'London' InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.units = 'metric'
ESQL to read a query parameter (clean, simple — no manual string parsing needed): SET location = COALESCE(InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.location, '');
Path segments from wildcard URLs (e.g. URLSpecifier="/api/*") are at: InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.Path.Segment[1] InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.Path.Segment[2] (etc.)
RULE: Every HTTP Input node that needs query parameters in ESQL MUST have parseQueryString="true" in the .msgflow XML. Without it, all reads return NULL and the flow silently misbehaves (no error, wrong data).
rule.correct_msgflow_example: <nodes xmi:type="ComIbmWSInput.msgnode:FCMComposite_1" xmi:id="FCMComposite_1_1" location="40,140" URLSpecifier="/weather/current" parseQueryString="true"> <translation xmi:type="utility:ConstantString" string="HTTP Input"/> </nodes>
rule.correct_esql_example: -- Works because parseQueryString="true" is set on the HTTP Input node SET location = COALESCE(InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.location, '');
rule.wrong_example: <!-- WRONG: missing parseQueryString — all query param reads will return NULL --> <nodes xmi:type="ComIbmWSInput.msgnode:FCMComposite_1" URLSpecifier="/weather/current"> <translation .../> </nodes>

rule.title: SOAP Input node mandatory attributes
rule.template: <nodes xmi:type="ComIbmSOAPInput.msgnode:FCMComposite_1" xmi:id="FCMComposite_1_1" location="20,20" wsdlFileName="MyService.wsdl" selectedPortType="MyServicePortType" selectedBinding="MyServiceSoapBinding" selectedPort="MyServicePort" targetNamespace="http://example.com/myservice/" useHTTPTransport="true" urlSelector="/MyService" allowQueryWSDL="true"> <translation xmi:type="utility:ConstantString" string="SOAP Input"/> </nodes>

rule.title: SOAP Request node mandatory attributes
rule.description: The mandatory URL attribute for SOAP Request is webServiceURL. Do not confuse with HTTP Request which uses URLSpecifier (see MF-08b).
rule.template: <nodes xmi:type="ComIbmSOAPRequest.msgnode:FCMComposite_1" xmi:id="FCMComposite_1_N" location="x,y" wsdlOperationMode="gateway" wsdlFileName="path/to/MyService.wsdl" selectedPortType="MyPortType" selectedBinding="MyServiceSoapBinding" selectedOperation="myOperation" selectedPort="MyPort" targetNamespace="http://example.com/myservice/" useHTTPTransport="true" webServiceURL="http://dummyUrl" sslProtocol="TLS" parserXmlnscBuildTreeUsingXMLSchema="false" validateMaster="none"> <translation xmi:type="utility:ConstantString" string="MySOAPRequest"/> </nodes>

rule.title: HTTP Request node — correct mandatory attribute, valid terminals, and dynamic URL
rule.description:
SOURCE OF TRUTH: MessageFlow.xsd ComIbmWSRequestNodeType (line 6600). Reference: xsd:attribute ref="iib:URLSpecifier" use="required"
── MANDATORY ATTRIBUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────── XML attribute name : URLSpecifier ← CORRECT Toolkit UI label : "Web service URL" Wrong attribute : webServiceURL ← WRONG (that belongs to SOAP Request)
Using webServiceURL on an HTTP Request node leaves URLSpecifier unset, causing: "Unset mandatory property Web service URL" in the Toolkit.
URLSpecifier MUST always be a non-empty URL string. Even when the runtime URL is overridden dynamically via OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.RequestURL in a preceding Compute node, URLSpecifier still holds the static default URL.
DO NOT use requestTimeout as an XML attribute — it is not valid for this node. Use timeoutForServer (optional) for request timeout configuration.
── DYNAMIC URL OVERRIDE (verified via ACE user trace) ─────────────────── Set the full URL including query string in a preceding Compute node: SET OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.RequestURL = fullBackendUrl; SET OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.RequestLine.Method = 'GET'; The HTTP Request node then uses this URL at runtime, overriding URLSpecifier.
── VALID OUTPUT TERMINALS (verified from schema) ──────────────────────── OutTerminal.out — backend returned HTTP 2xx (success) OutTerminal.error — backend returned HTTP 4xx or 5xx OutTerminal.failure — node-level failure (DNS failure, connection refused, etc.)
── INVALID TERMINALS — DO NOT USE on HTTP Request node ────────────────── OutTerminal.timeout — does NOT exist on ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode. Wiring it causes "Can not locate terminal" in the Toolkit. (timeout terminal exists ONLY on the HTTP Input node) OutTerminal.fault — does NOT exist on ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode. (fault terminal exists only on SOAP Request node)
── ON THE error TERMINAL — reading the backend response ───────────────── When the backend returns 4xx/5xx, the HTTP Request node routes to OutTerminal.error. At that point InputLocalEnvironment is empty (NULL root). The backend response is in: InputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" (integer status) InputRoot.BLOB.BLOB (response body as BLOB)
ESQL to pass the backend error response straight through: SET backendStatus = CAST( InputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" AS INTEGER); SET OutputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" = backendStatus; SET OutputRoot.BLOB.BLOB = InputRoot.BLOB.BLOB;
── ATTRIBUTE CONFUSION TABLE ───────────────────────────────────────────── ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode (HTTP Request) → mandatory URL attr = URLSpecifier ComIbmSOAPRequest.msgnode (SOAP Request) → mandatory URL attr = webServiceURL ComIbmWSInput.msgnode (HTTP Input) → URLSpecifier = inbound path pattern
rule.correct_template:
<nodes xmi:type="ComIbmWSRequest.msgnode:FCMComposite_1" xmi:id="FCMComposite_1_3" location="420,140" URLSpecifier="http://backend.example.com/api/endpoint"> <translation xmi:type="utility:ConstantString" string="CallBackend"/> </nodes>
<!-- Wire error terminal (HTTP 4xx/5xx from backend) --> <connections xmi:type="eflow:FCMConnection" xmi:id="FCMConnection_5" sourceNode="FCMComposite_1_3" targetNode="FCMComposite_1_Error" sourceTerminalName="OutTerminal.error" targetTerminalName="InTerminal.in"/>
<!-- Wire failure terminal (connection-level failure) --> <connections xmi:type="eflow:FCMConnection" xmi:id="FCMConnection_6" sourceNode="FCMComposite_1_3" targetNode="FCMComposite_1_Error" sourceTerminalName="OutTerminal.failure" targetTerminalName="InTerminal.in"/>

rule.title: ESQL module names must be globally unique within an ACE Application project
rule.description:
All .esql files in an ACE Application project share the same ESQL compilation scope (they are packaged into a single .appzip at build time). If two .esql files both define a CREATE COMPUTE MODULE with the same name, the Toolkit reports: "Unable to locate URN esql://routine/#ModuleName.Main" for one of the flows because the module name is ambiguous.
RULE: Prefix every module name with the flow name. Never use generic names like "BuildErrorResponse" or "SetHeaders" that would collide across flows.
CORRECT — flow-name-prefixed, globally unique: CurrentWeather.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildCurrentWeatherRequest CurrentWeather.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildCurrentWeatherErrorResponse WeatherAlerts.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildWeatherAlertsRequest WeatherAlerts.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildWeatherAlertsErrorResponse
WRONG — generic names that collide: CurrentWeather.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildErrorResponse ← AMBIGUOUS WeatherAlerts.esql → CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildErrorResponse ← AMBIGUOUS
The computeExpression in the .msgflow must exactly match the module name: computeExpression="esql://routine/#BuildCurrentWeatherErrorResponse.Main"

rule.title: connections elements — terminal name reference by node type
rule.description:
Every wire is a connections element. All xmi:id values must be unique (FCMConnection_N). sourceNode and targetNode reference the xmi:id values of the connected nodes.
CRITICAL: Terminals differ by node type. Using the wrong terminal name causes "Can not locate terminal" errors. The table below lists every verified terminal.
rule.template: <connections xmi:type="eflow:FCMConnection" xmi:id="FCMConnection_1" sourceNode="FCMComposite_1_1" targetNode="FCMComposite_1_2" sourceTerminalName="OutTerminal.out" targetTerminalName="InTerminal.in"/>

in.purpose: (not used — HTTP Input is a source node)

invalid.reason: Does NOT exist on this node type — wiring it causes Toolkit error
Does NOT exist on this node type

in.purpose: Receives the reply message to send to client
Receives HTTP error on fault path

out.purpose: Default output — RETURN TRUE propagates here
Second branch — fires after first completes

in.purpose: Exit point of the subflow (returns to caller)

rule.title: Subflow configurable properties require eStructuralFeatures and propertyOrganizer
rule.description: When a subflow exposes User-Defined Properties backed by ESQL EXTERNAL variables, declare each as an eStructuralFeatures before the translation element and register them in the propertyOrganizer section.
rule.template:
<!-- In eClassifiers, before translation: --> <eStructuralFeatures xmi:type="ecore:EAttribute" xmi:id="Property.DataServiceUrl" name="DataServiceUrl" defaultValueLiteral="http://dummyUrl"> <eType xmi:type="ecore:EDataType" href="http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore#//EString"/> </eStructuralFeatures>
<!-- In propertyOrganizer: --> <propertyOrganizer> <propertyDescriptor groupName="Group.Basic" configurable="true" userDefined="true" describedAttribute="Property.DataServiceUrl"> <propertyName xmi:type="utility:TranslatableString" key="Property.DataServiceUrl" bundleName="gen/find_Request_Response" pluginId="PolicySearch_Service"/> </propertyDescriptor> </propertyOrganizer>

rule.title: Real project reference flows in this workspace

file.pattern: HTTP Input (parseQueryString=true) + Compute (dynamic URL) + HTTP Request (URLSpecifier) + HTTP Reply. Root-level ESQL, no BROKER SCHEMA.
Same pattern as CurrentWeather. Two flows in one project — note flow-name-prefixed module names.
SOAP Input + SAP Request + common subflows. No BROKER SCHEMA.
SOAP service, RouteToLabel/Label, handler subflows, BROKER SCHEMA gen, cache Compute with dataSource.
Subflow with eStructuralFeatures UDPs, FlowOrder, multiple SOAP Request nodes, FCMSource/FCMSink.

rule.title: BROKER SCHEMA must match the file's subfolder path
rule.description: The BROKER SCHEMA value is the segment between "routine/" and "#" in every Compute node's computeExpression. - Root-level ESQL file: omit BROKER SCHEMA entirely. - File in a subfolder: BROKER SCHEMA statement is mandatory.

rule.title: ESQL module names must be globally unique within an ACE Application project
rule.description:
See MF-08c for full rationale. Applies equally at the ESQL level. All .esql files in a project share one compilation scope — duplicate module names cause "Unable to locate URN" errors in the Toolkit.
RULE: Always prefix module names with the flow name.
rule.example:
-- CurrentWeather.esql CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildCurrentWeatherRequest -- CORRECT: flow-prefixed CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildCurrentWeatherErrorResponse -- CORRECT: flow-prefixed
-- WeatherAlerts.esql CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildWeatherAlertsRequest -- CORRECT: flow-prefixed CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildWeatherAlertsErrorResponse -- CORRECT: flow-prefixed
-- WRONG: generic names that will collide if used in multiple flows CREATE COMPUTE MODULE BuildErrorResponse -- AMBIGUOUS across flows CREATE COMPUTE MODULE SetHeaders -- AMBIGUOUS across flows

rule.title: File-scope declarations: BROKER SCHEMA, NAMESPACE, EXTERNAL, SHARED
rule.description: All DECLARE NAMESPACE, DECLARE ... EXTERNAL, and DECLARE ... SHARED statements must appear at the top of the .esql file, OUTSIDE any module or procedure.

rule.title: Standard module header comment block
rule.description: Every CREATE COMPUTE MODULE must be preceded by a structured header comment.
rule.template: /******************************************************************************* * Node: NodeLabel * Module Name: ModuleName * * Description: What this module does. * * Ver Author Date Description * === ====== ==== =========== * 1 Name DD/MM/YYYY Initial ********************************************************************************/ CREATE COMPUTE MODULE ModuleName

rule.title: Every Compute module must include CopyMessageHeaders and CopyEntireMessage
rule.description: Include both helper procedures in every Compute module even if not explicitly called. CopyMessageHeaders() copies all message tree headers (excludes body). CopyEntireMessage() copies the complete message tree. Use RETURN FALSE when the module uses explicit PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL statements.

rule.title: Reading HTTP query parameters in ESQL
rule.description:
SOURCE OF TRUTH: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/app-connect/13.0.x?topic=nodes-httpinput-node
PREREQUISITE: The HTTP Input node MUST have parseQueryString="true" in the .msgflow (see MF-06b). Without it, all reads return NULL — no error is thrown.
CORRECT paths once parseQueryString="true" is set: InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.paramName
NEVER try to parse the query string manually from the HTTP command line. The X-Original-HTTP-Command header contains an absolute URI format for localhost requests (e.g. "GET http://localhost:7800/path HTTP/1.1" — NO query string), so manual parsing is unreliable and unnecessary.
Path segments from wildcard URLs (URLSpecifier="/api/*") are at: InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.Path.Segment[1] (first segment after wildcard) InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.Path.Segment[2]
rule.wrong_example:
-- WRONG: X-Original-HTTP-Command does NOT contain the query string for localhost requests SET httpCmd = InputRoot.HTTPInputHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Command"; -- Returns "GET http://localhost:7800/path HTTP/1.1" — no ?param=value
-- WRONG: QueryString child elements are NULL unless parseQueryString="true" is set SET location = InputLocalEnvironment.HTTP.Input.QueryString.location; -- NULL!

rule.title: Dynamic URL routing to a backend HTTP service
rule.description: Set the full backend URL (including query string) on OutputLocalEnvironment before the HTTP Request node. The HTTP Request node's URLSpecifier holds the static fallback URL but the Destination.HTTP.RequestURL value is used at runtime. Always set RETURN FALSE after explicit PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL calls.

rule.title: Handling the HTTP Request node error terminal in ESQL
rule.description:
When the HTTP Request node's OutTerminal.error fires (backend returned 4xx/5xx), InputLocalEnvironment is EMPTY (NULL root). Do NOT attempt to read from it. The backend response data is carried in InputRoot: InputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" — integer HTTP status InputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Line" — status line string InputRoot.BLOB.BLOB — response body as BLOB
To pass the backend's error response through to the client unchanged:

rule.title: Returning HTTP error responses to the client
rule.description: To set the HTTP response status code in an outbound HTTP Reply, set these fields BEFORE the HTTPReply node. The Toolkit uses X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code to control the actual HTTP status returned to the caller. Always CREATE the HTTPResponseHeader domain before setting fields on it.

rule.title: REFERENCE variable pattern and SHARED cache with TTL
rule.description: Use REFERENCE variables to avoid repeating long path expressions. Use SHARED ROW for in-memory caching of database lookups with timestamp-based TTL.

patterns.pattern: DECLARE inref REFERENCE TO InputRoot.SOAP.Body.ns1:getExchangeRate; DECLARE outref REFERENCE TO OutputRoot.SOAP.Body.ns1:getExchangeRateResponse.return;

rule.title: PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL and RETURN FALSE pattern
rule.description: Use PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL when a Compute node needs to route to a non-default terminal or to multiple terminals. Always follow with RETURN FALSE to prevent automatic propagation to OutTerminal.out after the function body returns.

rule.title: BAR file build command (ibmint package)
rule.description: Use ibmint package to build a BAR file from an ACE Application project directory. The ACE profile must be sourced first to put ibmint on the PATH. Source: /Applications/IBM App Connect Enterprise/server/bin/mqsiprofile (macOS)
rule.command: source "/Applications/IBM App Connect Enterprise/server/bin/mqsiprofile" ibmint package \ --input-path /path/to/workspace/MyProject \ --output-bar-file /path/to/workspace/BARfiles/MyProject.bar
rule.success_indicators: BIP1859I: Successfully added file ... to the BAR file. (one per source file) BIP1853I: Application file 'MyProject.appzip' successfully added to the BAR file. BIP8071I: Successful command completion.

rule.title: Deploy BAR to a running integration server via REST API
rule.description: The ACE admin REST API runs on HTTPS by default (use -sk for self-signed cert). Default admin port is 7600. Deploy with a POST to /apiv2/deploy.
rule.success_indicators: BIP9332I: Application 'MyProject' has been created successfully. (first deploy) BIP9332I: Application 'MyProject' has been changed successfully. (redeploy) BIP9326I: The source has been successfully deployed. HTTP:200

rule.title: Integration server HTTP listener ports
rule.description: The ACE integration server uses separate ports for admin and application HTTP traffic. Always confirm the actual ports before testing — they can be overridden in server.conf.yaml or via mqsichangeproperties.
rule.note: HTTP Input flows are always reached on the application HTTP port (7800 by default), NOT the admin port (7600). The admin port is for deployment and management only. Confirm the actual listening port from the server log: BIP3132I: The HTTP Listener has started listening on port '7800' for 'http' connections.

rule.title: Diagnosing runtime failures using ACE user trace
rule.description:
When a flow behaves unexpectedly at runtime, enable user trace via the admin REST API. The trace file is written to: TEST_SERVER/config/common/log/integration_server.TEST_SERVER.userTrace.0.txt
debugTree level shows full ESQL expression evaluations including variable values. This is the definitive way to diagnose wrong ESQL paths, NULL variables, and unexpected terminal routing.
rule.commands:
# Enable debug-level user trace curl -sk -X POST https://localhost:7600/apiv2/start-user-trace \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"traceLevel":"debugTree"}'
# Make a test request to capture in the trace curl -s "http://localhost:7800/my/endpoint?param=value"
# Stop user trace curl -sk -X POST https://localhost:7600/apiv2/stop-user-trace \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{}'
# Read the trace cat TEST_SERVER/config/common/log/integration_server.TEST_SERVER.userTrace.0.txt

key_trace_messages.message: Expression evaluation result — shows what a variable resolved to
Navigation failed — path element does not exist (field is NULL)
Assignment — shows value written to a field
HTTP Request node sending data — shows host and URL path
HTTP Request node received response — shows HTTP status code
Message propagated to named terminal (e.g. error, out, failure)
Message propagated from Compute node out terminal
Message propagated via PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL
HTTP Input node received request — shows method and path
